errors.observed_error: Three defects made the Windows desktop layer look impossible. (1) The harness called GetClientRect with three arguments (byref(w), byref(h)) against a two-argument API, so the whole RECT landed in the first pointer and width/height were read back as left/top = 0. Every window therefore measured 0x0 and the GDI proof returned windows=0 on a machine where the real main window measures 1280x820 and visible=true. (2) Because (1) kept `found` empty, PrintWindow and GetBitmapBits were never executed on any machine, hiding two further defects: the GDI/DC functions declared argtypes but no restype, so a raw int was passed where wt.HDC was required, and GetBitmapBits received ctypes.byref(c_size_t(n)) where a DWORD value was required - both raise 'argument 2: TypeError: wrong type' the moment the path is finally reached. (3) check_9 probed only shutil.which('cargo') and ~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe and then asserted 'Windows toolchain not installed' unconditionally, and GATE_SEMANTICS printed 'TAURI_WINDOWS_PENDING=yes(without Rust toolchain)'. That claim is false on this machine and contradicts the repository's own reference (windows-development-environment/references/tauri-build-shared-toolchain.md: 'Never turn a failed path probe into the persistent claim MSVC/Tauri is unavailable'), and register row AG-08 had promoted it to a machine-level blocker ('no Visual Studio and no VC tools at all').
errors.root_cause: Probe scope and dead code paths. The toolchain probe looked only at system PATH and the per-user cargo home, never at the declared shared roots in .project/governance/external-libraries-index.json (os-external), where MSVC 14.44.35207 (cl/link/MSBuild), a complete stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc toolchain with rustc.exe, cargo-tauri.exe and tauri-driver.exe all live; the Windows SDK import libraries are on the system volume at C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Lib/10.0.28000.0/{ucrt,um}/x64. Separately, a Win32 signature error made the GDI branch always return an empty set, so the two downstream ctypes defects were unreachable and stayed latent from the day the harness was written.
errors.fix: Corrected all three at the root. check_9 now resolves cargo through the declared shared roots (external-libraries-index.json sharedRoots + libraries[kind=toolchains].assets[tool=cargo]) after an optional WORKLAB_CARGO override, PATH and ~/.cargo/bin, and performs a real 'cargo --version' readback, reporting the resolved path and version; the false unconditional 'Windows toolchain not installed' string is gone and the pending reason now names what is actually outstanding (desktop WebView2 E2E not executed). GATE_SEMANTICS no longer asserts 'without Rust toolchain'. The harness's GetClientRect now takes (HWND, LPRECT) and is wrapped in _client_size, and the GDI call chain got the restypes it was missing (GetDC/CreateCompatibleDC -> wt.HDC, CreateCompatibleBitmap -> wt.HBITMAP, SelectObject -> wt.HGDIOBJ, GetBitmapBits -> c_ulong, PrintWindow -> c_bool) with the count passed as a value. Positive readbacks from the same round: the shared toolchain compiled and RAN an msvc-target binary with zero downloads (RUSTC_EXIT=0, RUN_EXIT=0, 251,392 B), the Observer built with BUILD_EXIT=0 in 1m30s (app.exe 9,779,712 B, sha256 e659bbe9b20a2677, PE imports api-ms-win-crt-*/dwmapi with no libgcc/libwinpthread), and the app now stays ALIVE against the real sidecar instead of early-exiting 0xC0000135 as the previous GNU artifact did.
errors.regression_test: A Win32 wrapper must declare argtypes AND restype for every handle-returning call, and value parameters must be passed as values; a probe may not report a toolchain as absent unless every declared location in .project/governance/external-libraries-index.json has been probed and its exact path recorded in the evidence.
errors.repeat_prevention: Never record a machine-level blocker from a single-path probe: enumerate the declared shared roots and Windows Kits first and cite the paths attempted. Environment-limited branches must be executed at least once, because a branch that is never reached cannot fail and therefore cannot be trusted.
errors.remaining_boundary: Not yet closed: the real desktop surface proof. CDP over the process-level WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS still yields no page target, so the probe window path (per-window additional_browser_args) is inert by architecture - WebView2 creates one browser environment per user-data folder and the main window creates it first. The corrected GDI proof has not yet produced a green verdict, so U19's desktop layer stays FAIL/PENDING and is not reported as passed. Full canonical gate after these edits: 47 gates PASS, exit 0.

(3) It forced SetWindowPos to a PHYSICAL 1200x800 while Tauri declares window size in LOGICAL pixels, shrinking the real CSS viewport from 1280x820 to 946x632 and changing the layout under measurement - at 946px the KPI grid reflows to two columns, so the four-across row that 'proved' the clipping no longer existed. errors.root_cause: The instrument reported numbers but never proved its own assumptions: which artifact it launched, whether that artifact was current, which rectangle it photographed, what coordinate space that rectangle lived in, and whether anything was on top of it. Each assumption was inherited from the previous run's guess, and every downstream breakpoint conclusion was stated as though measured. The one genuine layout defect the region did contain - .topbar reserving 210px for a cluster that is ~269 CSS px wide once the zoom group appears above 1240px, letting the transport truth strip slide under the caption buttons - was invisible because the captures never showed the real viewport.
errors.fix: New instrument .project-local/runs/p0a-diag-20261006/shot3.py: resolves the launched exe from every candidate target dir and refuses to run unless it is newer than tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml, src/*.rs and frontend/dist/** (STALE_OR_MISSING_BINARY otherwise); makes the process per-monitor-DPI-aware and records before/after; captures GetClientRect + ClientToScreen instead of GetWindowRect and fails if the client size disagrees with DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS by more than 3px; moves with SWP_NOSIZE so the app's own logical size is what gets judged; photographs the same rect twice, once by screen BitBlt and once by PrintWindow(PW_CLIENTONLY|PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), reports the differing-pixel ratio, and treats PrintWindow as authoritative when they disagree (occlusion) or the BitBlt is covered; parks the pointer outside the window before launch and restores it; and reports right-edge ink bands so clipping is measured rather than eyeballed. errors.observed_error: The GDI capture rectangle was derived from the comparison 'w * 12 >= WINDOW_LOGICAL_WIDTH_PX * dpi', a typo for * 96. On this machine GetClientRect already returns PHYSICAL pixels because the instrument had just made itself per-monitor DPI aware (main window reads 1600x1025 at GetDpiForWindow = 120, i.e. 1280x820 logical x 1.25), so the comparison wrongly concluded the value was still logical, scaled it by 1.25 a second time and allocated 2000x1281 for a 1600x1025 client area. BitBlt then copied 400x256 px of desktop and neighbouring windows past the subject's right and bottom edges. That foreign content made a window painting nothing but its own #08090a background read as 375, 635, 722 and 384 distinct colours across four windows, and a first-cut conclusion that the screen BitBlt had captured the real UI was recorded on that basis before the rectangle was checked.
errors.root_cause: The instrument inferred its coordinate space from a number instead of from the DPI-awareness state it had itself set, and it never bounded the capture rectangle by the client area it had measured microseconds earlier. Both failures point the same way: a capture larger than its subject photographs the surroundings and manufactures content that belongs to no application.
errors.fix: Scale is applied only when SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) did not take effect, and that fact is recorded per run as dpiAwareProcess. The requested rectangle is now clamped with min(w, round(w * scale)) and min(h, round(h * scale)), so it can never exceed the measured client area. Every window entry records sizeAsRead, captureSize, scaleApplied, dpi and expectedPhysicalWIfMain so the coordinate space is auditable after the fact.
errors.regression_test: python scripts/ci/failfast_group.py --group observer-python-skeleton plus the GDI stage of python apps/observer/scripts/u19_webview_e2e.py: every window entry must satisfy captureSize <= sizeAsRead. Re-running the corrected instrument against the same binary returned 41 distinct colours at #08090a 99.99% dominant, in place of the forged 375-722, which is the regression assertion.
errors.repeat_prevention: Every capture must record the coordinate space it believes it is in and the rectangle it used, and that rectangle must never exceed the client area measured in the same run; a capture larger than its subject must be rejected rather than read, because it photographs the desktop and forges evidence.
errors.remaining_boundary: Only the 1280x820 main and 440x780 panel windows were measured, so other resize states remain unmeasured. PrintWindow still cannot photograph the WebView2 surface (1-2 distinct colours across all four flags at both sizes), so the screen BitBlt remains the only working capture path and still depends on z-order.

errors.root_cause: Tauri v2 denies every mutating window and webview command by default. The compiled capability was [core:default, core:window:allow-start-dragging], and core:window:default in the build's own ACL manifest lists only readers (allow-is-maximized, allow-inner-size, allow-title and friends); allow-minimize, allow-toggle-maximize, allow-close and core:webview:allow-set-webview-zoom are separate identifiers that were never granted, so each click rejected at the ACL boundary. errors.observed_error: The freshness gate refused to run: STALE_OR_MISSING_BINARY because app.exe was older than src-tauri/Cargo.toml, whose mtime read 19:40:34 that evening. The same rule had already been defeated once in the other direction: it certified a binary built from a dist whose frontend/src had been edited half an hour earlier.
errors.root_cause: Freshness was keyed to filesystem mtimes on a working copy where git normalises line endings. The build's own output said it plainly: 'in the working copy of apps/observer/src-tauri/Cargo.toml, LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it'. Every such touch raises an mtime with zero content change, so the rule reports a stale binary for a file nobody edited, and it never compared frontend/src against frontend/dist at all, so a genuinely stale bundle passed. mtime is not content.
errors.fix: Content-keyed. An input raises the floor only when git sees a change in its bytes — `git diff --name-only HEAD` with the working-copy filters applied, plus untracked additions — so a file that matches HEAD contributes nothing and a content-free touch cannot move the gate; a deleted input fails closed. errors.observed_error: Six transport-truth properties the legacy suite pinned were absent in the production front: (1) the snapshot GET carried no cache directive, so a cached projection could be presented as current; (2) the response body was cast straight to SnapshotV3 with no structural check, so a legacy/v2 or truncated 200 response rendered as truth; (3) apply() overwrote unconditionally, so a delayed response with a LOWER revision replaced newer facts already on screen; (4) a browser-supplied ?api= was accepted as authoritative with no validation, so anything reachable from the webview (external host, https, credentials in the URL, an added ?write=1, a non-/api/v1 path) became the data source; (5) a payload read through the non-authoritative static-preview endpoint could set live=true and announce LIVE; (6) an EventSource error was an empty handler, so the surface kept its LIVE claim after the stream dropped, and a snapshot frame that failed to parse was swallowed without degrading.
errors.root_cause: The read path grew in one place (api.ts) while its contracts stayed in the retired static suite, so nothing in the production tree asserted them and no gate could notice the drift. Two of the six were the classic shape: an unvalidated cast of an external payload, and a trust decision delegated to the caller (the URL) instead of validated at the boundary. The three gate-side needle failures found while fixing this are the same class pointed at my own tests: the old clause read 'any fetch with an options object is suspicious' (which forbids the explicit GET the legacy contract required), a bare-text scan flagged the validator's own schema constant as an embedded snapshot, and an endpoint scan matched a module path (@tauri-apps/api/window) plus a regex replacement ('$1') as URLs.
errors.fix: fetchSnapshot now declares method:'GET' with cache:'no-store' and runs every body (SSE frames included) through parseSnapshotPayload, which fails closed. useLiveSnapshot tracks the last accepted revision and rejects a lower one without touching the displayed projection; a stream error or a corrupt snapshot frame stops the LIVE claim (the EventSource is never closed by us, so native reconnect survives); onOpen and resync_required schedule exactly one re-read, with bursts coalesced to one in-flight plus one follow-up; heartbeats cost no read; live is set only when the descriptor is authoritative AND the payload verdict is LIVE. isTrustedObserverEndpoint mirrors the Rust gate observer_api_is_loopback_get_only on the client side, and an untrusted ?api= is refused outright rather than being used or marked authoritative.
errors.regression_test: apps/observer/frontend/src/lib/transportTruthContract.test.ts (11 mounted-hook cases with a controllable EventSource stand-in) plus two new file-level cases in apps/observer/tests/test_production_surface_static_contract.js (viewport/320px floor, loopback-v1-only URLs). Falsified 15/15 with byte-for-byte restore and SHA-256 verification: falsify_transport_ports.py (query-guard removed, cache downgraded, schema check removed, monotonicity disabled, endpoint rotated from a payload field, authority gate removed, corrupt frame swallowed, coalescing disabled, onOpen not re-reading, refresh wiping the snapshot, stream error ignored) and falsify_step3_node.py (explicit GET dropped, snapshot literal embedded, off-loopback URL added, viewport pinned to width=1024).
errors.repeat_prevention: A read that crosses a process boundary needs three things at the boundary, not in the UI: an explicit method, a cache policy, and a structural parse that fails closed. Never accept an injected endpoint as authoritative without validating scheme/host/credentials/query/path; mirror the shell's gate in the client so a compromise of one layer is not enough. A needle written against source text must match the SHAPE of the violation (an assignment, a URL with a scheme) and must fail when it matches nothing, because a scan that silently matches zero files reads as a PASS. When a new compliant construct turns an old assertion red, adjudicate which is right before editing either - here the old clause was wrong, and the fix was to require the explicit GET rather than to forbid options.
errors.remaining_boundary: Not ported: the five brand SVGs still live only under apps/observer/web/assets/brand, src/theme/tokens.ts declares no read-only constraint block, the compact surface's dense project list is undecided, and the legacy 800/640 reflow breakpoints have no production analogue (the shell uses 840/1160/1240/1000 plus @container 820/900/760). The LIVE semantic now treats a stream error as 'not live until the next successful read', which is deliberately stricter than the poll-only model but has no timing guarantee shorter than pollMs.

errors.observed_error: The probe's own gate asked only that registrySha256 be 64 characters long, and the probe computed it over the working tree. Under `* text=auto` that value differs between this machine (CRLF) and the runner (LF), so the receipt's pin was unrepeatable across machines and could not be checked anywhere. It then went stale in a way I produced myself: after re-pointing hermes I ran the probe without --out, the printed summary was current while the shipped receipt still pinned the older registry and quoted the superseded version, and every test stayed green.
errors.root_cause: A digest claim was recorded without a basis and without a comparator. Length-64 reads as 'a hash is present' and hides both which bytes it names and whether the file still matches - the ERR-125 family, and the reason ERR-153 moved digest resolution to the index: the object that ships is the index blob, not the bytes on my disk.
errors.fix: registry_pin() now hashes the git index first, then HEAD, then the working tree, and names the basis in the receipt (git-index). The gate compares that pin against the same resolution and refuses a receipt that describes a different registry than the tree carries. Falsified by drifting the registry under a stale receipt (red) and restoring byte-for-byte (green again), and the assertion first fired on the real defect: the working-tree pin did not equal the index blob, which is the machine-dependence being removed.
errors.repeat_prevention: A published digest must state which object it names, and a gate must re-derive and compare it rather than check its shape. When a tool can run without writing its artifact, the artifact and the state it describes must be compared, or a fresh printout will silently coexist with a stale receipt.
errors.remaining_boundary: The comparison catches a receipt generated against different registry bytes; it does not detect a receipt that is current but whose *rows* were hand-edited, nor does it force anyone to re-run the probe with --out (running it without output still succeeds by design). The probe's per-row claims about binaries outside the repository remain machine-local and are readback-guarded, not CI-enforced.

errors.observed_error: A second adversarial pass over the surface committed in a279f54 found four defects that the canonical gate had gone green over. (1) `config.diff` answered `field in before` -- a substring predicate over the whole file -- for any path inside the repository, making every tracked and untracked file a content oracle one yes/no at a time. (2) The plane built `PermissionGate(Policy())`, whose default scope covers every ActionKind and whose forbidden lists are empty, and called `gate.evaluate(spec.action, target=request["operation"])`; the gate escalates a filesystem target naming .env/credential/secret/auth to CRITICAL, but an operation id contains none of those words, so the escalation branch was structurally unreachable and both implemented operations auto-allowed. (3) `_scope_failure` ran its containment test only `if candidate.is_absolute() and candidate.drive`, so a UNC boundary (`\\host\C$\x`, which Windows reports as neither absolute nor driven) and a drive-relative one (`E:secrets`) were accepted and recorded as granted scope in the ledger. (4) The identity check read the whole table under a per-process `threading.Lock` and then `upsert_task`-ed, whose ON CONFLICT branch copies lease_holder, lease_expires_at and fencing_token from the incoming record -- all absent for a control-plane create -- so a foreign replay wiped a live holder's lease and could send the fencing token backwards.
errors.root_cause: Every check was written against the threat I had pictured. The gate call was made to satisfy the sentence 'decisions are delegated to the permission gate' rather than to give that gate anything to look at; the diff was written as 'show me what changed' without asking what a yes/no answer can be used to learn; and the store's upsert was reused because it exists, not because conflict resolution by overwriting is what creating an identity means.
errors.fix: The diff answers a key-path question about a parsed document, returns UNKNOWN (never a boolean) when the document is not a mapping, refuses credential/session/database names and backup or evidence copies, and the gate now receives the resolved subject so its own CRITICAL escalation can fire; the policy scope is derived from the kinds the implemented operations declare, so adding an operation cannot widen it. Writes go through `insert_task_if_absent` (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, rowcount) and the conflict decision is made from the row that exists afterwards. Bound host, Host header and TCP peer must all be loopback by measurement rather than by name. Measured: 103 tests across test_control_service, test_planning_candidate_handoff, test_canonical_store, test_snapshot_task_records and test_adapter_capability_ladder run OK.
errors.repeat_prevention: A guard that is handed a constant is not a guard: any call that claims to delegate a decision must be checked for what it actually passes as the subject. Conflict handling is chosen per operation -- create, update and acquire are different transactions -- and a helper is not reusable just because it exists.
errors.remaining_boundary: The grant record is signed out of band and this service can only read it, which is the design and not a verified chain: there is no signature check, so a process that can write that file can authorise a candidate. `present_before` still discloses which top-level keys a diffable config declares. errors.observed_error: Two honesty defects in the read projection the same review reproduced on paper. `checkpointKeys` was built by iterating the checkpoint and stringifying it, which is only a key list when the value is a mapping: an array checkpoint projected its VALUES as key names and a bare string projected single characters, so user text reached a read-only snapshot under a field whose name promises metadata. Separately the store parsed the checkpoint column with `json.loads(raw or "{}")` and fell back to `{}` on failure, so a checkpoint that exists but will not parse was projected as `checkpointPresent: false` -- the snapshot asserting that nothing was stored. And the validator enforced 'no NATIVELY_VERIFIED without an observed execution layer' but never that the rungs below hold, so a card naming only OBSERVED_IN_EXECUTION=MET with a hand-written source validated clean.
errors.root_cause: The projection trusted its input's type because its own docstring said what it was supposed to contain, and an unreadable value was collapsed into the same empty value as an absent one because that is cheaper than representing two states. The ladder rule was written as a prohibition on a status word instead of as an ordering property over the layers.
errors.fix: The store now keeps a digest of exactly the bytes it stores plus an explicit parse state (ABSENT / PARSED / UNPARSEABLE), so presence survives a failed parse; the projection names keys only from a mapping and only those shaped like field names, and carries the stored digest as the identity for everything else. The validator requires layer names to come from the ladder and a MET rung to have every rung under it MET. Measured: 19 tests in test_snapshot_task_records and 21 in test_adapter_capability_ladder OK, including four new checkpoint-shape controls and two new ladder controls.
errors.repeat_prevention: A projection that filters or renames must state which types it accepts and refuse the rest; a digest is computed where the bytes live so the read side never needs the text. Ordering properties are validated as orderings, not as bans on individual words.
errors.remaining_boundary: A digest over a short checkpoint is low entropy and can be confirmed offline by anyone who can guess the payload; that was already true of the previous implementation and is not made worse. Key-name disclosure for a mapping checkpoint remains -- field names of workflow state are treated as metadata, which is a judgement a reader can reverse. The composition-root absent-vs-empty defect (a caught Exception returning an empty list) is fixed in the same commit's file but that file was mid-edit by another writer at commit time and is re-verified in the next round.
